writing-oathformula

Yahweh is following the custom of the culture by swearing an oath to indicate the seriousness of what he is saying. According to the custom, people would guarantee the oath by something that they hold sacred, and the most sacred thing would be the life of Yahweh. To do the same, Yahweh is swearing by his own life. Also according to custom, he is stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”), which would be the penalty for not telling the truth. Normally the penalty would be understood to be something general such as “may Yahweh punish me severely,” yielding something like, “If it is not because of my flock becoming prey…may Yahweh punish me severely.” But since Yahweh is speaking, stating this would not make sense. It may be clearest to translate the oath as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [I swear by myself…that it is because of my flock becoming prey]

nt: the earth will yield its produce
Alternate translation: [the earth will grow food] or [food will grow on the earth]
will be secure
Alternate translation: [will be safe]
know that I am Yahweh
figs-explicit

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 6:7](../06/07.md). Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]
when I break the bars of their yoke
figs-metaphor
Slavery is spoken of as if it were a yoke that people wear like some animals. Alternate translation: [when I free them from being slaves]
from the hand of those who enslaved them
figs-metonymy
Here “hand” represents power or control. Alternate translation: [from the control of those who made them slaves] or [from those who made them slaves]

they will not bear the scorn of the nations
figs-metonymy

Here “nations” represents the people of the nations. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **scorn**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form.
